family.description: This family includes members such as TrmO (tRNA-methyltransferase O) also known as YaeB, which contains a single-sheeted beta-barrel structure. TrmO is an AdoMet-dependent methyltransferase responsible for m6t6A formation [[cite:PUB00086552]]. Its human homolog, is responsible for formation of m6t6A37 in cytoplasmic tRNASer. Lack of TrmO decreases attenuation activity of the thr operon, indicating that N6 methylation of m6t6A37 ensures efficient decoding of ACY codons [[cite:PUB00137799]]. In bacteria and eukaryotes, TrmO has a C-terminal domain containing the conserved DPRxxY motif. Where the Asp194 and Arg196 in this motif of E. coli TrmO are necessary for N6-methylation. However, no archaeal YaeB has a C-terminal domain containing the DPRxxY motif that is conserved in bacterial and mammalian TrmO homologs [[cite:PUB00086552]]. This entry represents the N-terminal domain of TrmO.
family.name: tRNA-methyltransferase O N-terminal domain

record.description: This family includes members such as TrmO (tRNA-methyltransferase O) also known as YaeB, which contains a single-sheeted beta-barrel structure. TrmO is an AdoMet-dependent methyltransferase responsible for m6t6A formation [[cite:PUB00086552]]. Its human homolog, is responsible for formation of m6t6A37 in cytoplasmic tRNASer. Lack of TrmO decreases attenuation activity of the thr operon, indicating that N6 methylation of m6t6A37 ensures efficient decoding of ACY codons [[cite:PUB00137799]]. In bacteria and eukaryotes, TrmO has a C-terminal domain containing the conserved DPRxxY motif. Where the Asp194 and Arg196 in this motif of E. coli TrmO are necessary for N6-methylation. However, no archaeal YaeB has a C-terminal domain containing the DPRxxY motif that is conserved in bacterial and mammalian TrmO homologs [[cite:PUB00086552]]. This entry represents the N-terminal domain of TrmO.

evidence.explanation: Figures 3 and 6 support whole-protein mutation and biochemical effects. Protein abundance/folding, complete inserts and isolated-domain sufficiency remain unresolved; AF0241 contacts are not direct E. coli structural measurements.

discussions.notes: See the ledgers under evidence/PF01980. S5 and Table S2 confirm reference accessions and human primer endpoints, not complete inserts. The original reporter comparisons and assay-specific nulls are now assessed in qian1998-contexts.txt. They do not identify a direct decoding mechanism or resolve the older allele's sequence.

discussions.notes: Do not infer direct decoding, ribosome stalling, native transcription flux, human splicing regulation or universal zero activity from the scoped assays. The 1998 selection assay is itself a reporter proxy; its null result is not equivalence proof. Donor and crude-substrate label conflicts remain unresolved. Resolve source data and matched expression/folding controls before stronger conclusions.
